To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ratio of the forward amplitude to the total cross section, Re f/σt, has been measured at four incident proton momenta, 1.2 GeV/c, 1.3 GeV/c, and 1.8 GeV/c and 2.2 GeV.
the differential cross sections of elastic p p scattering have been measured at the CERN Proton Synchrotron (PS) at 1.20, 1.40, 1.80, and 2.60 GeV/c.

the ratio of the forward real to imaginary nuclear amplitude is measured for the first time at 1.8 GeV/c, that it is in agreement with theoretical predictions and that it is consistent with previous measurements at 2.6 and 3.6 GeV/ c.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elastic scattering of protons on protons at incident momenta between 1.2 and 2.5 GeV/c.
the elastic scattering of pions and protons on protons.
the study of the elastic scattering process of two nucleons at very low energies, in the energy range 0-1.5 GeV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the real part of forward scattering is well understood in the energy region covered by the present measurements.
there is no contradiction between the experimental results and the theory.
, within the experimental errors, no significant deviations from the theoretical predictions have been observed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the real part of our measured nuclear amplitudes is consistent with the predictions of the Glauber model, but the imaginary part is not.
the data do not contradict the predictions of the Glauber theory, and they are in reasonable agreement with it.
our data do not contradict the predictions of the dispersion relation theory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the forward amplitude of the p p elastic scattering is dominated by the Coulomb interaction at small angles.
the forward amplitude ratio, R, has a strong energy dependence.
the real part of nuclear amplitude at the forward angles is not negligible.
